description: Compute the electronic-energy reaction profile of sequential C-H scission of methane on the ferromagnetic Ni(111) FCC surface, using separately calculated *CHx and *H adsorption states to construct the intermediates and final *C + 4*H endpoint.
user_prompt: Compute the sequential C-H scission reaction profile of methane on the Ni(111) FCC surface (space group Fm-3m). Starting from gas-phase CH4 and a clean slab, four C-H bonds are broken sequentially on a single carbon center, constructing the *CH3 + *H, *CH2 + 2*H, *CH + 3*H, and *C + 4*H intermediate energies from separately calculated adsorption states. This is a thermal catalysis case; use gas-phase CH4 as the carbon reference and calculate CHx (x = 0-3) and H adsorption states separately using consistent slab models and calculation settings, adding the H contribution according to the number of dissociated H atoms. Build the full four-step ladder as intermediate context. Report the cumulative electronic reaction energy delta_E_total of CH4(g) + 5* -> *C + 4*H (in eV).
